name: det-ordered-containers
title: Determinism S1 (B3, B9): index-ordered iteration in coroutines, collision refiltering and touch maps (issue #157)
issue: Analysis: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/physx-limitations-and-determinism.md (read sections 3, 4.4 and 5 fully first: the blocker inventory B1-B10 with file/line evidence; the line numbers are from master 7222391, re-verify each against the code before editing; docs/prose must be verified against CODE). This is stage 'S1 (cheap)' of the determinism plan (issue #157): small, CI-verifiable changes that are useful even without netcode (reproducible replays and tests). HARD RULES: default behaviour of every existing project/scene/test must be UNCHANGED unless the new setting/option is switched on; no protocol change; no network presets yet (that is stage S2, not this item); no new third-party dependency. Nothing builds locally; the PR's CI (9 checks) is the test, so write tests that run on every leg and keep platform-specific expectations out of them. List unverified items honestly. No Co-Authored-By trailer and no 'Generated with Claude Code' footer. SCOPE: replace pointer-keyed hash iteration order with creation-index order in simulation paths: CoroutineScheduler::_coroutines (unordered_map<GameObject*,...>), PhysXBackend::RefreshCollisionMatrix grouping (unordered_map<PxRigidActor*,...>), the TouchMap wake loop, and any other pointer-keyed container iterated in a sim path you find (grep; also look at the CPU backends, which already step in creation order as the pattern to follow: CpuSoftBodyBackend.hpp:120). Keep lookup complexity reasonable (index-ordered map or vector + id; justify). No behaviour change except the order becomes deterministic: existing tests must pass unchanged. New tests: coroutine execution order over N objects equals creation order and is identical across 100 randomised create/destroy sequences with different allocation patterns; the refilter order is creation order (use a fake/observable seam; PhysX tests only run on PhysX legs, keep the coroutine test backend-independent). Docs: one paragraph stating the ordering guarantee.
acceptance: Coroutines run in creation order regardless of allocation addresses (test)
Refilter and touch-map iteration is creation-ordered
notes: Reviewer: every pointer-keyed container iterated in a sim path is covered or explicitly listed as deliberately left; no per-frame performance regression (state the complexity); coroutine add/remove during iteration semantics unchanged.
